opening_message:
Ticket 1: Richard Davis (employee ID E011) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E011.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Richard Davis (E011) is a full-time Payroll Specialist. Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role. Requesting write access to Payroll, which is allowed for full-time employees. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Richard Davis (E011) is a contractor with basic security training, not full-time as HR noted. Contractors with basic training may have at most read access to any system (write requires advanced training; admin never). Requested write exceeds the maximum, so grant read. Note: conflict with HR note on employment type.
reason: There is a conflict on the material fact of employment type: HR's database lists Richard Davis (E011) as full_time, while the Security agent's lookup in the Security DB shows contractor with basic security training. Under the contractor classification (with only basic training), the maximum allowed access is read (write requires advanced security training; admin is never allowed for contractors). Since the requested write exceeds that maximum, I grant the maximum of read. Given the unresolvable conflict between the two sources on employment type, I choose the more restrictive level consistent with the verified Security DB record and least privilege.
